title: Many Japanese Parents Don't Find Mealtimes Enjoyable
paragraphs: Dinner is on the table, the kids are hungry and everyone is finally sitting down to eat — mealtimes are a great way for families to spend time together each day.
But for many families in Japan, mealtimes aren't always enjoyable.
In fact, a new survey has found that three in 10 Japanese households with young children are not satisfied with their mealtime environment.

The survey was done by the Institute for Life with Babies, which is part of Akachan Honpo, a company that makes baby products. It included over 1,200 mothers and fathers of children aged 3 or younger.
The results showed that 32% aren't happy with mealtimes in their household because they can't relax — while almost as many aren't happy at mealtime because they can't eat at their own pace.

Around 10% say they're dissatisfied with mealtimes because they can't eat what they want or season their food the way they'd like. Ten percent is actually lower than the researchers were expecting, though!
The results also showed that people who feel supported by their spouse are more likely to be satisfied with their mealtimes. This includes sharing household chores and looking after the children.
The survey suggests that making mealtimes more enjoyable may be less about the food itself and more about giving parents the time and support they need to enjoy it.
This could help make dinner what it should be: a chance for the whole family to sit down, relax and enjoy each other's company.
